newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Roche says study backs Invirase for AIDS.
newsitem.headline: Roche says study backs Invirase for AIDS.

text.p: Pharmaceutical giant Roche said a major study had confirmed that a cocktial of three drugs, including its own Invirase, better prevented the outbreak of AIDS than standard two-drug treatment.

Roche said the 22-nation study found that adding Invirase to a treatment program for patients infected with the HIV virus reduced the outbreak of AIDS by 50 percent compared to using only the two standard drugs AZT and Hivid.
"This confirms what we knew from earlier studies and trials," Roche spokesman Roland Haefli told Reuters.
A Roche statement said it was the biggest and longest study yet comparing two-drug and three-drug cocktails, covering 3,485 patients between August 1994 and January 1997.
AIDS drugs work by targeting the HIV virus at various stages of its cycle of replication.
Invirase is one of a new generation of drugs called protease inhibitors that attack the virus late in the cycle, causing it to produce immature copies of itself which cannot infect other cells.
Roche said the study found that AIDS broke out in 76 of the patients who used the triple combination but in 142 of those who took the two-drug cocktail.

The outbreak of AIDS causes a patient's immune system to collapse, opening the door for such opportunistic infections as pneumonia, Kaposi's sarcoma or cytomegalovirus (CMV) and leading eventually to death.

Roche said the study's findings would be submitted to regulatory authorities in order to update the product labeling of Invirase, which has been approved in the U.S. since late 1995 and other major markets since earlyu 1996.
